howToSteps.name: Read the cups
howToSteps.text: Find the amount in cups in your recipe. A quarter, a third, a half, three quarters, or a whole number of cups are the usual amounts.

howToSteps.name: Multiply by 8
howToSteps.text: Cups times 8 gives fluid ounces. Half a cup is 4 fl oz, a full cup is 8 fl oz, two cups is 16 fl oz.

howToSteps.name: Read the jug scale
howToSteps.text: Most jugs are marked in both cups and fluid ounces. Read whichever scale the recipe uses and the other follows.

howToSteps.name: Do not swap in weight ounces
howToSteps.text: Fluid ounces are volume. A cup of flour is 8 fl oz but weighs about 4.25 oz. Only water is close to equal.

name: Cups to Fluid Ounces
title: US Cups to Fluid Ounces Converter
tutorial: One cup is 8 fluid ounces. The cup is defined as 8 fluid ounces, so this conversion is exact by definition, not by measurement. A cup measure and a jug marked in fluid ounces are the same tool with different lines on it.

Measuring jugs are where the conversion lives. Most American jugs are marked in both cups and fluid ounces, so a recipe that says 12 fl oz of broth is asking for 1 1/2 cups, and a recipe that says 3/4 cup is asking for 6 fl oz. Read whichever scale is easier and the other one follows.

The trap is weight. A cup of flour is 8 fluid ounces by volume, but it weighs about 4.25 ounces on a scale, because flour is light and full of air. A cup of water is 8 fluid ounces and weighs about 8.3 ounces. Fluid ounces measure how much space something takes up, and ounces measure how heavy it is, and the two only agree for water.

Drinks are the other home of fluid ounces. A standard can is 12 fl oz, which is 1 1/2 cups. A pint glass is 16 fl oz, which is 2 cups. A quart bottle is 32 fl oz, which is 4 cups. Once you know the can and the pint, the jug markings make sense.

Thirds are the one awkward case, the same as with tablespoons. A third of a cup is 2.67 fl oz, and two thirds is 5.33 fl oz. For drinks, round to the nearest half ounce. For baking, measure the third in tablespoons instead: a third of a cup is 5 tablespoons and a teaspoon.
